newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower but banks strong.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower but banks strong.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Friday with some profit taking ahead of the weekend, pushing the general index off its record high close on Thursday.
The Stockholm general index slipped 0.28 percent to 2,614.15 in a hefty day's trade in which shares worth 6.84 billion crowns changed hands.
The main focus of the day was the banking sector which defied the market's downwards trend to end 1.88 percent higher.
The interest came after commercial bank S-E-Banken posted its 1996 results showing a better-than-expected 68 percent jump in operating profit of 5.87 billion crowns.
"There was strong turnover in S-E-Banken and it seems a big investor from the U.S. was in the market and buying," said one broker.
S-E-Banken shares closed two crowns higher at 72.50 crowns after its shares worth 523 million crowns swopped owners.

Sweden's other three big banks, due to release 1996 earnings next week, also benefited. Nordbanken closed 3.5 up at 233 crowns, Swedbank SPAra.ST gained three to 119.5 crowns, and Handelsbanken rose three to 193 crowns.
The engineering sector lost 0.77 percent, reversing gains after Ericsson and Nokia posted results.
Ericsson closed 3.5 crowns lower at 245.5 crowns.

Insurer Skandia rose 2.5 crowns to 207 crowns after a rocky day's trade. The stock rose as much as seven crowns in morning trade after a Swedish newspaper said it was preparing to list its funds unit AFS. A company spokesman said nothing had been decided on this.
